title: Regional rotation gap leaves orphaned sessions and intermittent org-access denials for Dedicated clusters
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Several Dedicated customers reported intermittent 403s immediately after API key rotation events and during regional leader failovers. Errors surface as 'org-scope not found' and appear for a subset of requests routed to specific regional nodes. This ticket tracks root cause analysis, immediate mitigations, customer communications, and a long-term fix to ensure rotations+failovers are atomic with respect to org binding metadata.
reproduction_steps: 1) Use a Dedicated cluster with multi-region routing enabled and config 'edge_affinity' set to regional-preferred
2) Create an org-scoped API key and send traffic to create active sessions (live requests, KV cache entries).
3) Trigger a key rotation for the org via admin API while simultaneously initiating a leader re-election / rolling upgrade on a subset of regional nodes.

4) Observe ~0.1-1% of requests receive 403 with message 'org scope mismatch' for routes that previously succeeded. Failures concentrate on nodes that applied rotation events after metadata garbage-collection.
5) Verify tokens stamped with old key are still accepted on some nodes (stale cache) but rejected on others leading to intermittent access denial and session orphaning.
impact: High. Affected Dedicated customers experienced intermittent authorization failures for short windows (tens of seconds to minutes). This caused degraded user-facing flows and multiple customer escalations to Support and CSMs. No data exfiltration observed. Incident increased enterprise SLA risk.
root_cause: A race between the API key rotation propagation and regional metadata GC during rolling upgrades. Rotation writes updates to the central org->key mapping in the control plane and enqueues per-node update events. During leader failover/rolling upgrade one path used an async reconciliation window which allowed nodes to GC stale org bindings before they had applied the new rotation event. Additionally, our token-acceptance logic allowed opaque session tokens previously bound to the old key to be accepted if a node's local cache had not yet been reconciled, while other nodes immediately rejected them. This divergence produced intermittent 403s for identical requests depending on routing.
mitigation: Deployed a hotfix to the Dedicated control plane (release: dedicated-2026.02.3) that makes key rotation propagation synchronous for nodes undergoing leader election and pauses GC for org->key mappings until acknowledgment from all active regional replicas. Also added emergency runtime toggle 'rotation_strict_commit' to force consistent acceptance behavior during upgrades. Applied rollout to affected clusters during maintenance windows and monitored error rates.
short_term_steps_taken: Enabled rotation_strict_commit on all Dedicated clusters in impacted regions (NA/EU/APAC)
Paused rolling upgrades where customers reported incidents and re-applied updated control-plane images
Contacted CSMs and Support to notify affected customers and provide timeline and mitigation steps
Added temporary 2-minute grace window that accepts recently-rotated tokens while nodes reconcile to reduce customer visible errors
long_term_fixes: 1) Implement two-phase commit (2PC) style rotation: write -> quorum acknowledge -> commit, to ensure all regional replicas have consistent org-key mapping before GC proceeds
2) Replace ad-hoc local GC with versioned mappings and per-node reconciliation that tolerates out-of-order updates
3) Add end-to-end integration tests that simulate concurrent rotations + leader failover paths with realistic network partitions
4) Extend observability: add per-node rotation apply timestamps to dashboards and alert when variance > 5s
5) Update the SDKs and gateway routing policy to prefer recently-acknowledged nodes during known rotation windows

We underestimated the combinatorial effect of rolling upgrades + rotation events during peak traffic windows
Operational suggestion: avoid scheduling mass key rotations during cluster upgrades; coordinate via maintenance calendar until 2PC is implemented
